instagram.author: roiinmarketing
instagram.body:
Are you sick of people copying your content? Meta is disabling those who do it…
Are you tired of seeing your content being copied by someone else? Well, Meta is now banning, restricting, and disabling those accounts that do it. Here the Instagram Adam Mosseri just announced that they will be checking accounts over a 30-day period. And if those accounts are posting content that are the same as other creators, then they will be banned from being shown to anyone who is not their followers. Here's the catch: some creators are mentioning that they are getting flagged without even copying anyone. So, how do you check if your account has been flagged? Head to your settings and type in "status". There you'll be able to see whether you have been flagged or disabled on any content. And I mean, is this a good thing? Because if you're copying other creators' content directly, then maybe you should be banned. I don't know, what are your thoughts?

tiktok.author: itvnews
tiktok.body:
TikTok has launched a £3.99 subscription for users who don't want to see adverts on their platform Users will slowly begin to receive a message notifying them that they will need to be pay for an ad-free experience, as it is rolled out over the next few months. It's the latest social media company to make the move. Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat have already launched ad-free subscriptions. #ads #tiktokshop #adverts #adfree #news
If you're sick of scrolling through TikTok and coming across ad after ad, there will be a way to change that. But it comes at a price. TikTok has announced on May 11th that they're rolling out a new subscription called TikTok ad free for £3 99 a month. The social media giant said it will be rolled out over the next few months for account holders aged 18 or over. In the UK, if you don't opt in for the subscription, your account will stay as it is with personalised ads. And if you go for the subscription option, it will only remove the adverts delivered by TikTok across the app, like those pop up adverts with external links on your for you feed. It won't remove content posted by influencers or creators paid to advertise products or services, which may include an ad hashtag. TikTok is following in the footsteps of other apps like Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat who have all rolled out ad free subscription in the past few years. But currently on TikTok you can opt out of personalised ads which track your data. When the subscription option rolls out to you, that's something you'll have to pay for.

Just make sure you grab it before that sale is over.
